title: Coordinated outreach timetable and staffing rotations for product debut
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Create a single coordinated timetable and staffing rotation plan that aligns blog, email, social, webinar, and release-notes publication across Marketing, DevRel, Product, Support, and Eng. This ticket drives the operational playbook for execution day (T0) and the prep cadence (T-14 to T0). Deliverables: finalized timetable, owner roster per channel, approval checklist, embargo handling, measurement tags and dashboards, and contingency messaging for rollback or degraded service.
objectives: Ensure one canonical schedule for all public assets to avoid duplicate or conflicting announcements.
Define clear owners and backup owners for each channel with staffing rotations for T0 +/- 24h.
Lock down release notes content and publication windows, including localization and legal signoff timelines.
Instrument tracking (UTMs, dashboard events) and pre-wire analytics to measure reach and conversion.
Document contingency plans (soft launch, staggered region rollout, emergency pause) and who executes them.
success_criteria: All public assets (blog, email, social posts, webinar landing + recording) have owners and scheduled publish times in calendar by 2026-03-15.
Release notes are reviewed and approved by Product, Security, and Docs and staged in CMS by 2026-03-16.
On-call staffing rotation published and confirmed with Support and DevRel with contact tree and escalation steps.
Tracking links and dashboards are validated in staging and smoke-tested with sample events.
No channel publishes outside the embargo window; any deviation has an incident ledger entry.
timeline: T-14 (2026-03-06): Draft blog + release notes + webinar outline complete.
T-10 (2026-03-10): Initial cross-team review; this ticket created.
T-7 (2026-03-13): Final content draft for blog/email/social; localization brief submitted.
T-5 (2026-03-15): Content approvals due; calendar invites with publish timestamps sent.
T-2 (2026-03-18): Tracking/UTM smoke test; webinar dry run; backup owners confirmed.
T0 (2026-03-20): Publish window begins 15:00 UTC; coordinated social cadence and webinar at 16:00 UTC.
T+1 (2026-03-21): Post-mortem and metrics review; asset analytics snapshot.
tasks: Assemble canonical calendar and add to shared Drive: Marco to create calendar and invite all channel owners.
Lock release notes content in CMS and create translation tickets: Xiao to coordinate with Localization.
Draft announcement blog and 3-tier email sequence: Priya to draft, review by Product and Legal.
Prepare webinar landing page and registration flow, and rehearsals: Sarah to schedule two dry runs.
Create social copy variations and paid support plan: Damon to prepare copy and ad spends.
Prepare monitoring dashboard with top-level metrics: Rajesh to create and instrument events.
Set up UTM scheme and tracking spreadsheet: Marco and Damon to agree on naming conventions.
Define staffing rotation and create on-call list with phone/email: Mia to publish escalation steps.
Create contingency messaging (soft-launch, pause copy, outage notice): Marco to approve templates.
Schedule final content freeze and embargo enforcement checklist: Noor to own legal/approval signoff.
risks: Localization delay could push localized blog publishes out of sync; mitigations: staged publish windows per region.
Legal signoff not received by T-5: mitigation - publish English assets only with localized followups.
Tracking instrumentation breaks in production: mitigation - run smoke events and hold manual link backups.
High traffic causes degraded service on webinar registration: mitigation - pre-provision capacity and enable rate-limiter with fallback landing page.
notes: Embargo: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC. Press embargo exceptions require explicit approval from Noor; record any exceptions in the ticket.
PR template for publishing release notes: include changelog snippet, migration steps, and 'impact' banner for breaking changes.
Staggered social windows: 15:00 UTC, 15:15 UTC, 15:45 UTC for major platforms to reduce spike risk.
